item.title: NFP calls for removal of Christianity as a founding constitutional value and preservation of national common identity
item.description: The National Federation Party wants the removal of Christianity as a founding constitutional value of the State in Clause 1 of the Constitution Amendment Bill, while permitting appropriate historical recognition of Christianity and other faiths in the Preamble. The Party’s Management Board during its special meeting today discussed the Constitution Amendment Bill, identifying its shortcomings and
item.content:encoded:
The National Federation Party wants the removal of Christianity as a founding constitutional value of the State in Clause 1 of the Constitution Amendment Bill, while permitting appropriate historical recognition of Christianity and other faiths in the Preamble.

The Party’s Management Board during its special meeting today discussed the Constitution Amendment Bill, identifying its shortcomings and proposed changes that the Party believes are necessary.

NFP President, Parmod Chand says the party wants preservation of the common national identity of all citizens as Fijians, with equal political rights and constitutional protection for the identities, cultures and traditions of all communities.

They want absolute protection of iTaukei, Rotuman, Banaban and freehold land ownership, together with enforceable security of tenure for agricultural and residential tenants, including sublessees.

NFP wants a 56-member House elected through Mixed Member Proportional Representation, comprising 28 constituency members and 28 proportional representation members, with separate constituency and party votes.

They also want genuine representative Senate reflecting Fiji's diverse communities, without a majority of seats being controlled by the Bose Levu Vakaturaga.

NFP stressed removal of the provision permitting the lawful and moderate chastisement of children and complete removal of constitutional immunity provisions protecting those responsible for unconstitutional political upheavals and related conduct.

They want the removal of constitutional restrictions preventing citizens from seeking judicial remedies for unlawful or arbitrary actions of the State, depoliticisation of the Constitutional Offices Commission and the appointment of independent constitutional officeholders, enforceable constitutional provisions establishing the Ombudsman and requiring legislation on the Code of Conduct, accountability, transparency and freedom of information.

NFP wants strengthening of the Bill of Rights and removing excessive restrictions on freedom of expression, association, assembly, political participation and equality before the law, removal of any discretionary power of the President to determine when the Constitution comes into force, unambiguous constitutional subordination of the Republic of Fiji Military Forces to elected civilian authority, with no independent military mandate to intervene in government.

NFP wants an independent Constituency Boundaries Commission, fair electoral laws, transparent electoral administration and protection against political manipulation of elections, abolition of FICAC in its present form and the establishment of independent, accountable and effective arrangements for investigating and prosecuting corruption.

They want stronger constitutional safeguards against environmental degradation, protection of natural resources and provision for animal welfare, a fair, democratic and accessible constitutional amendment process, without permanent immunity provisions or disproportionate veto powers vested in any single institution and adequate time for public consultation, translation of the proposed Constitution into the vernacular languages, independent scrutiny and comprehensive parliamentary deliberation before its final passage.

The Party says these are principles upon which the NFP has stood for more than six decades.

NFP says it's support for the Constitution Amendment Bill and continued participation in the Special Parliamentary Committee on the Constitution is conditional and dependent on the extension of the timeline for public consultation until mid-December.

They say it will also depend on changes that the Party has identified and the principles that the NFP wants in the Constitution Amendment Bill are significantly important.

NFP is represented in Parliament’s Special Committee to review the Constitution Bill by its leader, Professor Biman Prasad.

NFP's President says the Government’s current timetable is for the Constitution Amendment Bill to return to Parliament in the first week of November and the Party is seriously concerned that of the 19 days, consultation is only for 13 days, 2 days is for Report writing and one day is to finalise the Report.

The Prime Minister indicated on Monday that he is prepared to look at a longer consultation and deliberation process, perhaps up to the end of the Parliament in late December.

Chand says NFP has consistently called for the replacement of the undemocratic 2013 Constitution, but replacing one Constitution with another cannot become another exercise in imposing constitutional arrangements upon the people without their informed consent.

He says Constitution's legitimacy must come from the people, not the political convenience of those in power.

item.title: Stories of survival move audience to tears at Leadership Fiji’s final leaders lounge
item.description: From being abandoned by his parents at a young age and living on the streets to building his own business, and to losing a job after 30 years of service, the stories of survival shared by Limitless Marketing Founder Asta Sonner and Nadro Events Solutions Director Mili Naituyaga moved the attendees to tears at Leadership Fiji’s final Leaders Lounge event. Held under the theme Legacy Through Story,
item.content:encoded:
From being abandoned by his parents at a young age and living on the streets to building his own business, and to losing a job after 30 years of service, the stories of survival shared by Limitless Marketing Founder Asta Sonner and Nadro Events Solutions Director Mili Naituyaga moved the attendees to tears at Leadership Fiji’s final Leaders Lounge event.

Held under the theme Legacy Through Story, the event brought together friends and alumni of Leadership Fiji, providing a platform for the two entrepreneurs to share their journey of overcoming adversity and rebuilding their lives.

Sonner inspired the audience with his story of growing up without parental support, living alone on the streets and eventually rising above his circumstances to become the director of his own business.

Naituyaga, the wife of the late former Fiji 7s player Aminiasi Naituyaga, also known as the Steelman, shared her experience of being made redundant by Fiji Airways after 30 years of service, reflecting on the challenges she faced following the unexpected turn in her career.

Chief Executive Officer of Leadership Fiji, Sharyne Fong, thanked the participants for being part of the organisation’s programmes from the beginning of the year through to the final event.

Fong says the safe space created through the Leaders Lounge had encouraged members to inspire others and build a future grounded in resilience by drawing strength from the challenges they had faced.

The event highlighted the importance of storytelling in preserving experiences, strengthening identity and passing on valuable lessons and knowledge to future generations.

item.title: Serevi considers entering politics ahead of next general elections
item.description: Speaking on fijivillage Straight Talk with Vijay Narayan, Serevi says he is thinking about doing something new to help Fiji move forward. Insert: Serevi joining Politics 14th Oct 26
item.content:encoded:
Speaking on fijivillage Straight Talk with Vijay Narayan, Serevi says he is thinking about doing something new to help Fiji move forward.

Insert: Serevi joining Politics 14th Oct 26

He says there are many youth who need guidance and opportunities, and he would be willing to enter politics if given the chance to make a difference.

When asked which political party he is planning to join, Serevi says he is still weighing his options.

He mentioned Unity Fiji among the parties he has been looking at but stressed that no political party has attracted him enough to make a decision.

Serevi says some parties have approached him for meetings, and he is looking forward to having discussions with them.

He says he remains open to speaking with different political parties before deciding on his next move.

Meanwhile, Serevi says his main concern is the future of Fiji's young people, particularly with the growing problems of drugs and HIV in the country.

He says this was one of the main reasons he returned to Fiji after spending many years overseas.

Serevi says he has been back in the country for about 18 months and has already spoken to around 35,000 to 40,000 young people through schools, churches, villages and rugby clubs.

He says his programmes focus on motivating young people, encouraging them to stay away from drugs and helping them set goals for their future.

Through the Serevi International Academy of Rugby, he is also working with boys and girls aged 15 to 18, using rugby to develop their skills and help them become better people.

Serevi believes everyone has a responsibility to help address the challenges facing young people, including parents, community leaders, sportspeople and those in government.

Serevi warns that if people do not work together to address these problems, the situation could become worse in the next five to ten years.

He also believes Fiji needs more unity, saying people should focus on helping one another and building the country rather than bringing others down, particularly on social media.

item.title: Police call for change in road safety mindset following fatal accidents along Navua
item.description: Following the death of two men in Nabukavesi along Queen’s Highway last night and an eight-year-old in Vakabalea in August in separate accidents, and calls for more measures to prevent accidents, Police say people’s behaviour and mindset must change. Police say both men who died last night were 26 years old, with one being a police officer who was on his day off and travelling home to Nabukavesi.
item.content:encoded:
Following the death of two men in Nabukavesi along Queen’s Highway last night and an eight-year-old in Vakabalea in August in separate accidents, and calls for more measures to prevent accidents, Police say people’s behaviour and mindset must change.

Police say both men who died last night were 26 years old, with one being a police officer who was on his day off and travelling home to Nabukavesi.

The second victim was a salesman who resided in Navua.

Based on initial information gathered, Police say it is alleged that the salesman overtook several vehicles along a double line before the collision occurred.

Police say this is subject to ongoing police investigations.

We are noticing a lot of speeding and overtaking at the bends despite oncoming traffic on our highways.

Vakabalea residents in Navua have also been calling on authorities to introduce more speed control measures along the Vakabalea main road, where residents say several accidents have already occurred.

While responding to fijivillage News, Police say they will continue to call for a change in mindset towards road safety among everyone, including drivers, pedestrians, parents and guardians, particularly when it comes to children, as road safety is everyone’s responsibility.

They say Police and Land Transport Authorities officers are doing their part, and are out conducting operations, bookings and awareness on our roads, everyday.

Police add the onus is on all road users.

item.title: US Embassy yet to respond on whether evidence against Zhao Fugang has been shared with Fiji Govt
item.description: Mansi Chand , Navitalai Naivalurua , Vijay Narayan · 14/10/2026 The United States Embassy is yet to respond to questions on whether it has shared credible evidence with the Fiji Government regarding Zhao Fugang's alleged involvement in significant corruption on behalf of China-based actors.
item.content:encoded:
Mansi Chand , Navitalai Naivalurua , Vijay Narayan · 14/10/2026

The United States Embassy is yet to respond to questions on whether it has shared credible evidence with the Fiji Government regarding Zhao Fugang's alleged involvement in significant corruption on behalf of China-based actors.

Following the release of the notice, the Fiji Government encouraged the United States authorities to share credible information or evidence of alleged offences committed in Fiji with their Fijian counterparts for assessment and investigation, where warranted.

The US State Department says the designation makes Fugang and his immediate family members generally ineligible for entry into the United States.

It alleges that Fugang abused his public position by paying bribes to Fijian citizens to advance the interests of China-based government, business and criminal actors.

The Department says his alleged actions constituted significant corruption and adversely affected US interests in Fiji.

The Fiji Government had earlier highlighted that any allegations of unlawful conduct within Fiji must be addressed through the appropriate Fijian legal and law enforcement processes.

Fugang has denied the allegations, stressing that they are unsubstantiated.

Fugang added that he respects the laws of Fiji and will cooperate fully with any lawful inquiry by the Fijian authorities.

item.title: St John’s College girls’ hostel stove repaired, fundraising needed for boys’ hostel stove
item.description: Students at the girls' hostel of St John's College in Cawaci, Ovalau, can now have their meals prepared using the hostel's stove, which is fully repaired and operational after months of fundraising. Principal Alosio Saukuru confirmed to fijivillage News that the repairs were made possible through fundraising by the Lautoka-based St John's College Old Scholars Association.
item.content:encoded:
Students at the girls' hostel of St John's College in Cawaci, Ovalau, can now have their meals prepared using the hostel's stove, which is fully repaired and operational after months of fundraising.

Principal Alosio Saukuru confirmed to fijivillage News that the repairs were made possible through fundraising by the Lautoka-based St John's College Old Scholars Association.

The school had been relying on firewood to prepare meals for students at the girls' hostel after the stove broke down last year.

Saukuru says the association is now fundraising for repairs to the cooking facilities at the boys' hostel, which are also showing signs of deterioration.

He says the association is targeting November to begin work on the boys' hostel stove, subject to the funds raised.

Anyone wishing to assist or make a donation can contact Saukuru on 2029875.
